changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: I will fold.
changes.after: I'll fold.

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: I do not want to know! ...damn it...
changes.after: I don't want to know! ...damn it...

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: The window is shut exactly as it was. A careful culprit.
changes.after: The window is shut exactly as it was. The culprit was careful.

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: First class to the captain's cabin. Good. I can retrace it.
changes.after: From first class to the captain's cabin. Good. I can retrace the route.

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: What is with this man? Out of nowhere...
changes.after: What's with this man? That came out of nowhere...

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: What is with Kirikov?
changes.after: What's with Kirikov?

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: Open your ears and listen carefully.
changes.after: Listen carefully.

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: They as good as said it.
changes.after: They all but said so.

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: You drew the picture in the Center Hall well.
changes.after: You did a fine job on the picture in the Center Hall.

changes.speaker: Ilyu
changes.before: It is not such special work. There are any number of similar jobs.
changes.after: It's not such unusual work. There are plenty of jobs like it.

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: The candidates are down to two: you and Kirikov. I will bet on you.
changes.after: There are only two candidates left: you and Kirikov. I'll bet on you.

changes.speaker: Ilyu
changes.before: What is wrong? Is that bravado from moments ago gone?
changes.after: What is wrong? Where did all that bravado go?

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: Are you lost about something?
changes.after: Do you feel lost?

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: Either one. No doubt.
changes.after: It must be one of them.

changes.speaker: Ilyu
changes.before: Is that fun?
changes.after: Are you enjoying this?

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: Maybe. But can one person directly see what another is thinking?
changes.after: Maybe. But can one person see directly into another person's thoughts?

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: This is no time to leisurely list your asylum terms!
changes.after: This is no time to list your asylum terms at leisure!

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: I bet on my favorite bluff.
changes.after: I used my favorite bluff.

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: Let us begin. The screwdriver...this one...
changes.after: Let's begin. The screwdriver...this one...

changes.speaker: Ilyu
changes.before: Calm down. I am with you. Right?
changes.after: Calm down. I'm right here with you. All right?

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: Let us open the box's left lid.
changes.after: Let's open the left lid of the box.

changes.speaker: Ilyu
changes.before: To enter the court and uncover which courtiers secretly harbored treason against him.
changes.after: To enter the court and uncover which courtiers secretly harbored treasonous intentions against him.

changes.speaker: Kasuke
changes.before: ...one more...Tainui Adjell's assassin is hiding aboard.

notes.source: High-confidence PROPOSED EDIT rows from the Japanese-verified localization audit, filtered against the post-source-correction canonical branch by exact before-text match.
notes.selection: 23 exact matches retained from 75 exact-speaker Kasuke/Ilyu candidates; 52 stale candidates were rejected to prevent overwriting later semantic corrections.
notes.Kasuke: Natural educated conversational English, with contractions and blunt phrasing under pressure; no invented regional dialect or faux-Victorian register.
notes.Ilyu: Educated cosmopolitan English, playful or emotionally direct where the Japanese supports it, while retaining a more controlled intelligence-officer register when appropriate.
notes.punctuation: ASCII punctuation only; PART3C:059 uses a straight apostrophe for game-font compatibility.
